The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—rose by 6.8 points to 121.2, following three months of consecutive decline. results.title: US Consumer Confidence Edged Down Slightly in August

results.content: The decline was driven by a drop in the Expectations Index, which measures consumers' six-month outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions. That gauge fell 5.8 points to 68.2, more than offsetting a 6.8-point rise in the Present Situation Index to 121.2 — the first improvement in that measure in four months. An Expectations Index reading below 80 is generally associated with a recession within the next year, the Conference Board noted.
